transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello. Um... well, I suppose I'm here because I've been having trouble just... staying put. Like during staff meetings, or at dinner. I just keep getting up when everyone else is seated. 

I'll... I'll suddenly feel like I need to refill my coffee, or go check a handout at the back of the room. Even though nothing is really urgent. So... yes, that's mainly it.
When you're at home alone, or doing something you really enjoy, do you find yourself having this same difficulty sitting still, or does it mainly happen in situations like meetings and dinners?

Well... yes, I suppose it happens then, too. Even if it's just a quiet evening with my husband, watching a movie... or at my book club. 

I find it hard to just sit quietly with the book or the film. Before I know it, I'm... making comments, or rustling around in the kitchen. Or just suggesting we do something else entirely. So... yes, it's not just at work.

When you feel this urge to get up and move around, is it more like an uncomfortable feeling of tension or anxiety inside your body that you need to release, or is it more like your mind just feels scattered and you can't focus on sitting still?

I'm... not entirely sure. I haven't really thought about it that way. It's just... I just feel like I need to move. I don't know if it's tension or just... my mind. It's just a feeling that I can't stay sitting.
How long have you been experiencing this difficulty sitting still? Has it been something you've noticed your whole life, or is this something that started more recently?

I'm... not really sure about my whole life. But it's been noticeably harder to manage recently. Maybe for the last eight months or so. 

Um... my youngest left for college around then. The house is just... quieter now. So I suppose that's when it really started standing out.

Besides this difficulty sitting still, have you been experiencing excessive worry or anxious thoughts about things—either about specific concerns or just a general sense of worry that's hard to control?
No, not really. I mean... I wouldn't say I'm excessively worried. Just the normal things, I suppose. Nothing that feels out of control.
When you feel this urge to move around, do you notice any physical sensations like your heart racing, sweating, or trembling in your body?
No... I don't think so. I haven't noticed my heart racing or anything like that. Just... just the need to get up.

Besides this difficulty sitting still, have you been preoccupied with your health or noticed any other physical symptoms in your body that have been bothering you—things like pain, fatigue, or other bodily sensations?
No... I haven't. I mean, my health is fine. I don't really dwell on it, so... no. Nothing like that is bothering me.

You mentioned your youngest left for college about eight months ago, and that's when you really started noticing this restlessness. Do you feel like this difficulty sitting still is directly connected to missing your child or adjusting to an empty house, or does it feel more like a separate issue that just happened to become more noticeable around that time?

I suppose... it's just a separate thing. I miss him, of course, but... it doesn't feel like it's about that. The house is just quieter now, so maybe it's just easier to notice when I'm pacing around. But it's not because I'm upset about him leaving.

When you're sitting still and feeling this urge to move, do you ever feel disconnected from your body or surroundings, like you're watching yourself from outside, or does the world feel unreal or distant to you?
No... no, nothing like that. I'm just... I'm just sitting there, wanting to stand up. It doesn't feel strange or distant. Just restless.

When you get this urge to stand up and move around, is there something specific going through your mind—like a thought or worry that makes you feel you need to get up—or does it just feel like a physical restlessness without any particular thought attached to it?
No, there's no... specific thought. I don't really worry about anything in particular. It's just... physical, I guess. I just feel like I need to move. That's all.

When you feel this urge to move around, do you notice any involuntary twitching, fidgeting with your hands, or repetitive movements that you feel compelled to do—or is it more just a general restlessness without specific movements?

I guess... I do fidget some. Not twitching, really. Just... tapping my foot, or clicking my pen. I notice it mostly when I'm sitting at my desk grading essays. Or... in church. I end up shifting around so much I just have to remind myself to settle down.

When you get that urge to move or fidget—like tapping your foot or clicking your pen—does it feel like there's an uncomfortable sensation in your legs or body that the movement helps relieve, or is it more just a habit or preference to move?
I don't think so. It's not... uncomfortable, really. I just do it without thinking about it. It's not like I'm trying to fix a feeling in my legs. It's just... what I do.
Looking back to when you were a child or teenager in school, do you remember having this same difficulty sitting still and fidgeting with things like pens or your hands back then?

I suppose... yes. It's not a new thing. I remember my old report cards usually said I was bright, but... that I couldn't stay in my seat. Or wait my turn. 

My mother actually used to joke about it. She'd say I wore a path between my desk and the pencil sharpener before I was ten. So... I've always been like this, I guess.
